procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Delhi at New Delhi
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 30.03.2011 of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in LPA No. 810 of 2010.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Delhi issued a Judgment and Order on 30.03.2011 in LPA No. 810 of 2010.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court addressed multiple Criminal Appeals and Special Leave Petitions (SLPs) related to the case.  It allowed some appeals to be withdrawn without prejudice, dismissed others, set aside the impugned order in Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013 and remanded the matter to the High Court for fresh decision in accordance with law in view of judgment of this Court dated 28th March, 2018 in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation, Criminal Appeal NO(s).1375-1376 of 2013, detagged one SLP, and tagged another. The Supreme Court directed parties to appear before the trial court or High Court for further proceedings, depending on the specific case.

decision.appeal_result: Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013 is dismissed as infructuous. Criminal Appeal Nos. 1386-1387 of 2013, 1395 of 2013, and SLP (Crl.) No(s). 10050-10051/2013 are dismissed on merit. Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013 is disposed of, with the impugned order being set aside and the matter remanded to the High Court for fresh decision. All other connected appeals and special leave petitions are allowed to be withdrawn without prejudice.
directions: The parties are directed to appear before the trial court or High Court on the specified dates for further proceedings.
The record in all the matters is to be sent to the trial court so that the trial court may proceed with the matters pending before it.
SLP(Crl.) No(s). 5678/2014 is detagged and to be listed independently.
SLP(Crl.) No. 9363/2017 is to be tagged to SLP(Crl.)NO.6165 of 2016.

issue.issue_text: Whether Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013 had become infructuous.

facts: The counsel for the appellant(s) in Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013 made a statement to the Supreme Court.
law: An appeal is considered 'infructuous' when the underlying issue has been resolved or no longer exists, making a judicial decision on the matter unnecessary.
A court can accept the statement or concession of a party's counsel as the basis for its decision.
application: The Supreme Court accepted the statement from the appellant's counsel that the appeal had become infructuous.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013 as infructuous based on the statement made by the counsel for the appellant(s).

issue.issue_text: Whether the challenges raised in Criminal Appeal Nos. 1386-1387 of 2013, 1395 of 2013, and SLP (Crl.) Nos. 10050-10051/2013 had any merit.

application.text: The Supreme Court reviewed the specified criminal appeals and special leave petitions and determined that they had no merit.
application.sentence_text: We do not find any merit in these appeals and the special leave petitions which are hereby dismissed.

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeals and special leave petitions, finding they lacked merit. The Court also directed the parties to appear before the trial court for further proceedings.

issue.issue_text: Whether the impugned order in Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013 should be set aside and the matter remanded to the High Court for a fresh decision in light of the judgment in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation.

facts: The Supreme Court was considering Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013.
A recent judgment had been delivered by the Court on March 28, 2018, in the case of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation.
law: The Court's decision was based on its own precedent set in the judgment of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation.
application: The Court applied the legal principles from the Asian Resurfacing judgment to the order being challenged in Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the impugned order and remanded the matter to the High Court for a fresh decision. This new decision must be made in accordance with the law established in the Asian Resurfacing judgment. The parties were directed to appear before the High Court on May 28, 2018.

issue.issue_text: Whether the appellants/petitioners in the other connected appeals and special leave petitions should be allowed to withdraw their cases.

facts: The appellants and petitioners in a number of connected criminal appeals and special leave petitions sought to withdraw their cases from the Supreme Court.
law: A party to a legal proceeding can typically request to withdraw their case. The court has the discretion to grant this request.

A withdrawal can be granted "without prejudice," which means that the party withdrawing the case does not forfeit their right to raise the same legal arguments or issues in a different or lower court proceeding.
application: The Supreme Court reviewed the requests from the various parties.
For a large number of the cases, the Court explicitly stated, "The appeal is allowed to be withdrawn without prejudice to any contention to be raised before the trial court in accordance with law."

By granting the withdrawal "without prejudice," the Court ensured that the appellants/petitioners were not disadvantaged by their decision to withdraw from the Supreme Court and could continue to argue their points as the case proceeded in the trial court.
The Court also ordered the parties in these cases to appear before the trial court on specified dates to continue the proceedings.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the requests and allowed the appellants/petitioners in the specified cases to withdraw their appeals and special leave petitions. The Court granted this withdrawal "without prejudice," preserving the parties' rights to raise their arguments in the trial court, and directed them to appear before the trial court for further proceedings.

arguments.issue_text: Whether Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013 had become infructuous.
appellant_arguments: The counsel for the appellant stated that the appeal had become infructuous.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the challenges raised in Criminal Appeal Nos. 1386-1387 of 2013, 1395 of 2013, and SLP (Crl.) Nos. 10050-10051/2013 had any merit.
appellant_arguments: The appellants argued that their appeals and special leave petitions had merit and should be allowed.
respondent_arguments: The respondents likely argued that the appeals and petitions lacked merit and should be dismissed.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the impugned order in Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013 should be set aside and the matter remanded to the High Court for a fresh decision in light of the judgment in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation.
appellant_arguments: The appellant argued that the matter should be reconsidered in light of the recent judgment in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation, which warranted setting aside the impugned order and remanding the case to the High Court.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the appellants/petitioners in the other connected appeals and special leave petitions should be allowed to withdraw their cases.
appellant_arguments: The appellants/petitioners in various connected cases requested to withdraw their appeals and special leave petitions.

cases.case_name: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. and Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation
cases.principle: As the binding precedent based on which the impugned order was set aside and the matter was remanded to the High Court for a fresh decision.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: In view of the judgment in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation, a matter may be remanded to the High Court for a fresh decision in accordance with the law established in that precedent.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court disposed of a batch of connected criminal appeals and special leave petitions on various grounds. The central substantive action was to remand one specific appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013) to the High Court for reconsideration based on the recent three-judge bench ruling in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation. Other appeals were dismissed either on the merits without elaborated reasoning or as infructuous based on counsel's statement, while the remainder were permitted to be withdrawn.
legal_tests_applied: The court applied the precedent established in the judgment of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency P. Ltd. And Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation, [2018] 2 SCR 1045, to determine the outcome of Criminal Appeal No. 1394/2013.
why_appellant_lost: In Criminal Appeal Nos. 1386-1387 of 2013, 1395 of 2013, and SLP (Crl.) No(s). 10050-10051/2013, the appellants lost because the court made a conclusory finding that their cases lacked merit, stating: 'We do not find any merit in these appeals and the special leave petitions which are hereby dismissed.'
In Criminal Appeal No. 1384 of 2013, the appellant lost because the appeal was rendered moot, as the court dismissed it 'as infructuous on the statement of learned counsel for the appellant(s).'
why_respondent_won: In the appeals and special leave petitions dismissed on the merits, the respondent prevailed because the court agreed that the challenges raised were without substance, although the specific reasoning for this conclusion was not articulated in the order.
